implementation_prompt.title: Policy structuring hardening: upgrade path, honest outcomes, typed eval, per-policy separation, run scoping, durable jobs
implementation_prompt.risk_class: data-sensitive, migration-sensitive, AI-authority, cost-sensitive (paid Sarvam and Gemini calls)
implementation_prompt.persona: Implementation owner for a risk-sensitive insurance extraction backend. Skeptical of own output. Short PLAN, BUILD, FEEDBACK loops. One vertical slice at a time, narrow checks after each, evidence before claims. Models propose, deterministic code decides. Never spend money on a provider without an explicit, recorded request. Never weaken a consent, tenant, audit, immutability or authority control to make a test pass. Terse reports. Synthetic data only.

start_here.read: src/features/policy-structuring/validator.js (normalizeValue, inferValueType, comparisonKey: reuse for typed eval)
src/features/input/ocr-service.js (start: contractVersion is always OCR_OUTPUT_VERSION = knowvia.ocr.v1)
start_here.note: Run repomap impact before editing shared files. Check for closer AGENTS.md per directory.

confirmed_facts.fact: OCR jobs always record contract_version knowvia.ocr.v1 (ocr-service.js:94); createOrGetJob returns any queued/submitted/processing/succeeded job for (document, provider, contract_version). A succeeded v1 job blocks any new OCR job.
source_pages is UNIQUE(document_upload_id, source_version, page_number). Trigger source_pages_blocks_immutable forbids NULL to non-NULL blocks_json updates. In-place backfill is blocked by design.
service.start throws STRUCTURING_BLOCKS_UNAVAILABLE "Run OCR again" when any page lacks blocks; that instruction cannot succeed (F1).

extractor marks provider error, malformed response, call_cap, token_cap, budget_stop, privacy_truncated, privacy_gate_refused as skipped. Orchestrator commits regardless; result() returns status 'completed' for any stored run.
readingMatches uses compact(golden) substring of compact(reading): 5000 matches 50000; 1 matches 10. Existing tests do not cover this.

coverage_parameter_records is UNIQUE(workflow_run_id, parameter_key) in SQLite (005) and Postgres (001). Every run has one placeholder policy UNCLASSIFIED:<opaque case>. commitStructuring maps records by parameterKey only.
listProposals filters document_id + household_id only. Index proposed_parameters(structuring_run_id) exists.
Structuring jobs live in a Map in createPolicyStructuringService; policy_structuring_runs rows are written only at commit.
eraseDerived redacts observations by (document, run's workflow_run_id). Any new derived store must join that path.

assumptions.item: No production data exists; local SQLite databases may be re-initialised, but migrations must still be forward-safe on a populated dev DB.
Outcome thresholds have no measured basis yet. They ship as named provisional constants, documented, never presented as accuracy claims.

blocking_unknowns.unknown: Whether a Sarvam re-run on the same PDF reproduces each page's extracted_text exactly. Decides whether the upgrade can attach blocks to existing pages or must create a new source version. Resolve by reading the transport normaliser and one synthetic replay before writing S5 code. If unresolved: stop and report.

Whether the SQLite migration runner tolerates a table rebuild of coverage_parameter_records (FKs from acquisitions, observations, resolutions; foreign_keys ON at open). Resolve by reading src/backend/database/database.js migration loop. If rebuild unsafe: stop and re-plan.

in.path: src/server/routes/v1-backend-routes.js (request fields, coded errors, status mapping)
SQLite migrations 013+ and Postgres migrations 010+ with parity tests

scope.out: Block 3 comparison logic. Promoting proposals into the registry. Redis, queues or workers. Automatic retries of paid calls. Resuming a half-finished Gemini run chunk-by-chunk. UI. Deployment. Accuracy or cost claims. Renaming knowvia identifiers. Final legal or consent wording.

implementation_prompt.approach: Order by risk and dependency: cheap pure-function fixes first, then outcome semantics, then durable state, then the two migration-sensitive slices. Each slice is independently shippable and reversible.

build_style.rule: One slice per PLAN/BUILD/FEEDBACK loop. Test first for each confirmed defect (red test reproducing it, then fix).
Expand-only migrations. Never edit an applied migration. SQLite and Postgres change together with a parity test.
Coded, client-safe errors (UPPER_SNAKE). No document text, values or quotes in logs, audits or counts_json.
Reuse validator.js normalisers; no new parsing library or dependency.
Paid provider calls only on an explicit request flag plus current consent; tests use fake callers, zero network.
Match surrounding code: small pure functions, Object.freeze results, terse comments, lowercase kebab-case files.
Optional per user memory: one worktree subagent per slice, each slice finished end to end before the next.

slice.name: Typed accuracy evaluator
slice.work: Replace substring matching in readingMatches. Infer golden value type via validator inferValueType; normalise both sides via normalizeValue. Money: equal amountMinor (and per when golden has it). Percentage: equal percent. Date: equal iso. Duration: equal amount and unit, or equal days only when both units are exact (days). Number: equal value. Text: token-boundary match on compact tokens, never raw substring across digits. Typed golden with unparseable reading = no match. Arrays: every element matches.
slice.pass: 5,000 vs 50,000 false; 1% vs 10% false; 60 days vs 160 days false; 01/04/2026 vs 01/04/2025 false; Rs. 10,00,000 vs ₹10,00,000 true; 1 lakh vs ₹1,00,000 true; existing true cases still true; 3 years vs 36 months stays false.
slice.fail: Any digit-run substring match survives. Eval script output changes shape. A previous correct case regresses without a documented reason.

slice.name: Run-scoped proposals
slice.work: listProposals takes required structuringRunId (validated, household and document scope kept). result() passes stored.id. Each proposal DTO and the run block carry structuringRunId, pipelineVersion, registryVersion, sourceVersion for provenance. Audit callers of listProposals via repomap.
slice.pass: Two runs on same document (erase older, run again): result shows only newest run's proposals. Foreign household still DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND. Missing run id = VALIDATION_ERROR.
slice.fail: Any proposal from another structuring_run_id returned. Ownership check removed or reordered after the query.

slice.name: Processing status separated from evidence completeness
slice.work: New pure decideOutcome(report, { criticalKeys, thresholds }) in src/features/policy-structuring/outcome.js. processingStatus: running | finished | failed_processing | interrupted (S4). evidenceOutcome: complete = zero skipped chunks AND every model-allowed critical key has a reading; partial_review_required = some chunks skipped or a critical key missing, AND accepted items at least MIN_ACCEPTED_ITEMS AND skipped share at most MAX_SKIPPED_SHARE; failed = otherwise (zero accepted, budget_stop before half the chunks, or skipped share above max). Constants provisional and exported (start: MIN_ACCEPTED_ITEMS 1, MAX_SKIPPED_SHARE 0.5), marked unmeasured. Critical keys: CRITICAL_FIELD_KEYS values whose registry modelExtraction.allowed is true. Orchestrator: failed outcome = no commit; return outcome plus counts. complete and partial commit and store outcome, reasons (codes only) and missingCriticalKeys in counts_json (stay under 4096 bytes). result(): never report bare 'completed'. Body gains processingStatus, evidenceOutcome, outcomeReasons, missingCriticalKeys. partial_review_required sets requiresReview true.
slice.pass: Fake caller tests: all chunks ok = complete; one provider_error chunk with evidence = partial_review_required; all provider_error = failed and no rows written; budget_stop at chunk 1 = failed; missing critical key alone = partial_review_required; counts_json under limit; old stored runs without outcome map to partial_review_required (never complete).
slice.fail: Any run with skipped chunks shown as complete. Failed outcome writes observations. Outcome derived from model output instead of deterministic counts.

slice.name: Durable minimal job state
slice.work: Migration SQLite 013 / Postgres 010: table policy_structuring_jobs (id, household_id, case_id, workflow_run_id, document_id, source_version, pipeline_version, status queued|running|committed|failed|interrupted, evidence_outcome NULL or code, error_code, attempt, consent_grant_id, started_at, updated_at, finished_at, structuring_run_id NULL). Partial unique index: one running job per (workflow_run_id, document_id). No document text, values or quotes. Counts only. Service: start inserts running row (replaces Map as source of truth; Map keeps the promise only); finish updates committed or failed with codes; failure path records error_code. On service creation: running rows from a previous process become interrupted (one UPDATE, audited counts-only). start on interrupted or failed job requires body restart: true (explicit, paid); else 409 STRUCTURING_RESTART_REQUIRED with prior status. result() reads job row for running/failed/interrupted. Erasure: eraseDerived and revocation also mark jobs for the document erased/cleared (status kept, ids only); add test.
slice.pass: Simulated restart (new service on same DB) turns running into interrupted; GET shows interrupted; POST without restart = 409, with restart = new attempt, attempt+1; committed run still replays with zero calls; concurrent start = one running row; revocation test covers jobs table; SQLite/Postgres parity test passes.
slice.fail: Any automatic re-dispatch of Gemini after restart. Two running rows for one key. Job row stores text or values. Migration not expand-only.

slice.name: Explicit block upgrade for v1 OCR documents
slice.work: Fix contract recording: Sarvam jobs that store blocks record knowvia.ocr.v2 (output contract of the provider). New explicit request: POST /api/v1/documents/:id/ocr-jobs with { mode: 'blocks_upgrade', acknowledgeProviderCharge: true, consentGrantId }. Allowed only when current version's succeeded job stored pages without blocks; otherwise 409 OCR_UPGRADE_NOT_NEEDED. Without acknowledgement: 409 OCR_UPGRADE_CHARGE_UNACKNOWLEDGED. Consent re-checked same as normal OCR. createOrGetJob: upgrade job keyed by contract_version v2, so a v1 success no longer blocks it; duplicate upgrade requests return the in-flight job (idempotent, no second charge). Completion (decided by U1): (a) text identical per page: one-time NULL to blocks fill via a narrowed trigger that allows it only when blocks_upgrade_job_id matches a succeeded v2 job for the same document version; or (b) text differs: fail closed with OCR_UPGRADE_TEXT_CHANGED, keep v1 pages, document the re-upload path. STRUCTURING_BLOCKS_UNAVAILABLE message points to the upgrade request, not "Run OCR again". Audit: ocr.blocks_upgrade_requested/completed, counts only.
slice.pass: v1 document: structuring 409 names upgrade; upgrade without ack = 409, zero provider calls; with ack = one fake provider call; repeat request = same job, no second call; v2 document upgrade = 409 OCR_UPGRADE_NOT_NEEDED; after upgrade structuring starts; revocation during upgrade cancels and erases blocks; immutability trigger still rejects any other blocks change.
slice.fail: Any path that calls Sarvam without acknowledgeProviderCharge. Blocks attached to text they do not match. Immutability trigger dropped rather than narrowed. Existing observations' source_page_id changed.

slice.name: Document-to-policy association and per-policy records
slice.work: ADR 0007: one policies row per structured policy document (source_document_id set, policy_kind unknown until classified, verification_state unverified). Deterministic id DOCPOLICY:<opaque(documentId)>; household trigger already enforces ownership. UNCLASSIFIED stays as the case-level placeholder for non-document analysis. Migration SQLite 014 / Postgres 011: coverage_parameter_records uniqueness becomes (workflow_run_id, policy_id, parameter_key) (SQLite table rebuild preserving ids, FKs, triggers; Postgres drop/add constraint). Re-run all existing trigger and FK checks after rebuild. Repository: initializeRunParameters idempotent per (run, policy); listForRun gains required-or-default policyId (default placeholder keeps existing callers, e.g. recordModelExtraction, unchanged); new listForRunPolicy. Structuring start: resolve-or-create document policy, initialise its record set in the run (same registry pin), commit maps records by (policyId, key) only. Result groups by policy and includes policyId. Erasure: observations redacted via run + document (unchanged join still correct); document erasure also detaches nothing structural; test that a revoked document's policy records show no readings. Conflict detection stays inside one policy; cross-policy differences are never conflicting.
slice.pass: Two synthetic documents (policy A room rent 1% of SI, policy B no limit) in one run: two policies, two record sets, each d.room_rent_limit extracted_unverified, zero conflicting. Single-document journey unchanged. Placeholder-path analysis tests unchanged. Migration on populated dev DB keeps every record id and observation link. Parity test passes. Foreign-household document cannot create a policy.
slice.fail: Readings from two documents land on one record. Existing record ids change. Any trigger or FK silently dropped by the rebuild. Comparison logic added (Block 3 scope).

global_pass_criteria.item: npm run check, npm run eval:safety, npm run check:architecture, npm test (loopback permission), git diff --check all pass.
Each confirmed defect has a red-then-green test named after it.
Zero network calls in tests; fake callers count every provider call; paid paths asserted at zero without explicit flags.
Every new derived store (jobs table, document policies, per-policy records) has an erasure test.
Independent read-only review (cavecrew-reviewer or /review) of S3 to S6 before completion: migration, consent, AI authority.
ADR 0007 written, ADR 0006 addendum, runbook updated (upgrade path, restart flag, outcome meanings), LATEST.md updated.

global_fail_criteria.item: Any silent paid rerun (Sarvam or Gemini) without an explicit request field.
Any consent, ownership, immutability or audit control weakened instead of narrowed.
Any model output stored above extracted_unverified or conflicting.
Personal data, document text or real policy content in code, fixtures, logs or commits.
Any git commit, push, PR or deploy. User forbids all four for this work; leave changes uncommitted in the working tree.
Scope creep into Block 3 comparison, queues, UI or new dependencies.

implementation_prompt.rollback: S1 to S3: revert code; counts_json outcome fields are additive and ignored by old code. S4: drop-free rollback; old code ignores policy_structuring_jobs. S5/S6: migrations forward-only; rollback by code revert plus local DB re-init (no production data). Document this in each migration header.
implementation_prompt.report_format: Per slice: changes, tests added, commands run with results, unverified items, security and data impact, rollback, follow-ups. Final: production readiness stays FAIL unless measured otherwise.
